predictions.mechanism: GCC security rhetoric preserves a geopolitical risk premium, but no new military action, sanctions, or shipping disruption was announced.
predictions.invalidation: A concrete new attack on GCC infrastructure or shipping would shift gold risk upward; a verified de-escalation agreement would weaken the safe-haven impulse.

predictions.mechanism: The statement reinforces Gulf geopolitical risk but does not materially change supply, policy, or military facts yet.
predictions.invalidation: A fresh attack or renewed oil spike would turn the equity bias bearish; concrete de-escalation and falling oil would turn it bullish.

predictions.mechanism: Geopolitical risk is a headwind, while the absence of a new actionable escalation limits directional conviction; high yields remain an independent valuation pressure.
predictions.invalidation: A fresh regional escalation plus higher oil and yields would turn the setup bearish; verified de-escalation would improve the risk outlook.

predictions.mechanism: Europe is sensitive to energy risk, but this statement alone adds rhetoric rather than a new supply disruption.
predictions.invalidation: A renewed oil spike tied to a concrete Gulf disruption would make the setup bearish; sustained de-escalation and cheaper energy would improve it.

learning_application.basis: ACTIONABLE v2 confidence calibration shows low-confidence directional predictions underperform while low-confidence MIXED/neutral segments perform strongly; because current facts are rhetorical rather than a new concrete escalation, the profile supports MIXED 4/10 rather than forcing a directional call.
